text.p: Australia thrashed Tahiti 5-0 in an Oceania group World Cup qualifying match on Friday to maintain Terry Venables' perfect record since becoming national coach last year.
Australia have maximum points from two games after routing Solomon Islands 13-0 on Wednesday and appear certain to cruise into a play-off to decide the Oceania winners.
South Melbourne striker Paul Trimboli, one of nine changes made by Venables to the starting line-up on Friday, scored twice in the match at Parramatta Stadium.
Tenerife striker Aurelio Vidmar, Graham Arnold, who plays for Hiroshima in the Japanese J-League, and defender Matt Bingley from Sydney national league club Marconi shared the other goals.
It was the former England coach's seventh victory in as many matches since he replaced Eddie Thomson last November to guide Australia's World Cup campaign.
"Tahiti made more of a game of it (than Solomon Islands), and they put a lot of bodies behind the ball. It wasn't easy. But you've got to give a bit of credit to the opposition," Venables said.
Australia are hosting the qualifying tournament in Sydney after Tahiti and Solomon Islands agreed to surrender home advantage. The second legs will be played on the same ground next week.
New Zealand are expected to qualify from the other group. The Oceania play-off will be played over two legs in June and July.
The winner will play an Asian opponent in a final two-leg qualifier later this year for a berth in the 1998 World Cup finals in France.
